newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 16.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company -- LLOYDS TO INCREASE CAPITAL REQUIRED BY NAMES

In a move to strengthen its financial security and credibility, Lloyds bank is proposing that Names - individuals whose assets traditionally backed Lloyds - increase the amount of capital it puts up to support underwriting activities. Some believe Names may interpret the move as an attempt to drive them out of the market in favour of new corporate investors.
-- BAE ACTS TO CALM FRENCH AIRBUS ANXIETY

Amid concern in France that European aerospace consolidation would lead to closure of its factories and research centres, British Aerospace has made a statement reassuring the country that business would continue as usual when it becomes a limited company in 1999. John Weston, BAe's managing director, said the Airbus changes should precede a single European aerospace and defence company which would retain national identities. BAe also said preservation of national identities was more important in defence than in civil aircraft manufacturing.
-- EUROPEAN CAR SALES DISTORTED BY INCENTIVES

Due to lower automobile registration levels in March, carmakers have raised concern that sales in 1997 will be well below expected levels. Many manufacturers believe demand may have been distorted following last year's government and industry incentive schemes which pulled sales forward in France and Germany. France's sales were down 21.2 per cent and Germany's 8.6 per cent, while the schemes had the opposite effect in Italy, with sales increasing by 25.1 per cent.
-- US NATURE PUBLISHER SETS UP TV VENTURE

The publishers of National Geographic magazine, the National Geographic Society, have made the announcement that the UK will be the site for the launch of its first TV channel. The channel is to feature nature and documentary programming and will be launched on satellite and cable in August, as a joint venture with British Sky Broadcasting. National Geographic currently shows programmes throughout North America and other regions of the world.
-- CHANNEL 5 CHIEF PRAISES SUPPORT OF ADVERTISERS

Following all of its airtime in April being sold prior to the March 30th launch, Channel 5's chief executive, David Elstein, has praised "fantastic support" by advertisers. The television station is optimistic of earning between 70 and 80 million stg in advertising revenues during its first nine months, far higher than predicted. Company sales director, Nick Milligan, announced that advertising competition has finally arrived to UK television, which will result in quality TV for less for advertisers and improved programming for the viewer.
-- OECD HIGHLIGHTS MANUFACTURING SUCCESS

According to unpublished figures from the Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development, UK industries including cars, chemicals, aircraft and oil refining have become industry leaders in productivity growth since the late 1980s. The results demonstrate evidence of improvement in performance for many UK manufacturing groups, spurred on by new management ethics which aim to improve quality and teamwork. Across all manufacturing sectors, Britain was second only to Japan in productivity performance.
-- DEAL ON 9 BILLION STG ON EUROTUNNEL DEBT

The operator of the cross-channel rail link Eurotunnel has finalised the restructuring of its 9 billion stg debt by the steering committee of leading bankers ahead of approval by its instructing banks due later this month. This restructuring has been announced a week before Eurotunnel's annual results are released which allows shareholders to vote on the plan in July prior to discussions by the company's syndicate of 225 banks at the end of the year. The final version of the restructuring plan has only been marginally changed since it was initialed in October by Eurotunnel and its bankers.
-- JOHN MOWLEM TO FLOAT 49 PER CENT OF SGB OFFSHOOT

Construction group John Mowlem is to announce plans to float 49 per cent of its SGB scaffolding-to-ladders offshoot today. This placing is thought to value the business at 100 million stg, and Mowlem, who bought the business for 160 million in 1996, will use the finance raised to fund the early redemption of a 50 million eurobond and invest the remainder in other areas of the company. SGB, founded in 1903, is one of the world's largest companies involved in selling and hiring equipment for construction.
-- 90 MILLION STG SHARE BUYBACK PLAN TAKES CITY BY SURPRISE

Anglo-US engineering group LucasVarity announced the unexpected decision of a larger-than-expected 150 million stg share buy back scheme. The first report since the company's merger of Lucas Industries and Varity Corporation, valued at 3.2 billion stg in 1996, states that the group intends to spend 90 million stg buying shares back as well as 40 million stg on an annual dividend of 4.5p. The group decided on this split buy-back and dividend policy as the decision to abandon dividends was rejected.
-- AUDIENCE APPLAUDS CONCERT OVERTURE

The merger of BT and US MCI was overwhelmingly welcomed by BT's 2.3 million shareholders on Tuesday as 831 shareholders congregated at Wembley Conference Centre to receive the news from BT chairman Sir Iain Valance that the merged company Concert would be "the world's best market defender and the world's best market attacker". On Tuesday Portugal Telecom reported an alliance with BT and MCI which would allow Concert sole distributorship for services in Portugal.
